title: Optimization Is The Key Challenge For Quantum Computing
gist: Dell CTO John Roese frames quantum computing as a staged, engineering-driven ramp: enough error-corrected logical qubits for molecular-level optimization (materials, batteries, drugs, corrosion) around 2028-29, then large-scale logistics optimization by ~2030, while Dell, HPE, Cisco and IBM build hybrid quantum-classical datacenter infrastructure.

insights.claim: McKinsey said in April 2026 that quantum computing had reached a commercial tipping point, with investors putting $12.6 billion into quantum startups the prior year.
insights.speaker: Jeff Burt
insights.so_what: Rising venture flows indicate quantum is entering a commercialization phase investors must track.

insights.claim: Companies in climate and life sciences, travel and logistics, and financial services are already using quantum computing to optimize processes, test scenarios and run simulations.
insights.speaker: Jeff Burt
insights.so_what: Early adopter verticals indicate where first quantum revenue pools will form.

insights.claim: Quantum computing will not be a flip-the-switch moment but a steady march toward scalable fault-tolerant systems with steadily improving error-corrected qubits, architectures, software and applications.
insights.speaker: John Roese
insights.so_what: Argues for gradual value capture rather than a binary breakthrough, favoring patient positioning.

insights.claim: Quantum computing is no longer a physics problem but an engineering one.
insights.speaker: Jeff Burt
insights.so_what: Shifts risk from scientific feasibility to execution and scaling, a more investable profile.
insights.quote: Quantum computing is no longer a physics problem, but an engineering one.

insights.claim: Dell, HPE, Cisco and IBM are putting infrastructure in place for hybrid quantum-classical HPC datacenters, with Cisco building a quantum-focused networking architecture.
insights.speaker: Jeff Burt
insights.so_what: Incumbent IT vendors position to capture integration spend as quantum enters datacenters.

insights.claim: HPE announced partnerships with IQM, Quantinuum, QuEra and Rigetti to integrate their quantum systems with HPE's Cray supercomputers, and Equal1 showed its RacQ system at Dell Technologies World 2026.
insights.speaker: Jeff Burt
insights.so_what: Quantum hardware vendors are aligning with OEM channels, a route to enterprise distribution.

insights.claim: Architectures from Qarakal Quantum and Infleqtion aim to reduce the number of physical qubits needed per logical qubit, cutting infrastructure and energy costs, reducing noise and easing co-location with classical HPC.
insights.speaker: Jeff Burt
insights.so_what: Qubit-efficiency improvements could pull forward timelines and lower deployment cost.

insights.claim: Around 2028-2029 there will likely be enough error-corrected logical qubits to tackle the first batch of real problems, which are molecular-level optimizations.
insights.speaker: John Roese
insights.so_what: Sets a concrete near-term window for first useful fault-tolerant quantum workloads.
insights.quote: before the end of this decade, so in like 2028, ‘29, we will likely have enough error-corrected logical qubits to go after the first batch of real problems

insights.claim: Material properties such as corrosion resistance depend on the atomic arrangement within molecules, so quantum optimization of atomic spacing and binding could design corrosion-free materials; Roese cites estimates that corrosion costs the global economy a trillion dollars a year.
insights.speaker: John Roese
insights.so_what: Points to a large addressable value pool for quantum-enabled materials science.
insights.quote: corrosion costs the global economy a trillion dollars a year

insights.claim: Drug discovery and longer-lasting batteries also fall under molecular-level optimization that quantum systems can do faster and at greater scale than traditional supercomputers.
insights.speaker: Jeff Burt
insights.so_what: Pharma and battery chemistry are early beneficiaries to watch for quantum partnerships.

insights.claim: By the start of the next decade, quantum systems should be capable of large-scale optimizations such as airline and transportation coordination and financial-firm problems, with logistics currently the largest opportunity.
insights.speaker: John Roese
insights.so_what: Logistics, airlines and finance are the second-wave addressable markets around 2030.
insights.quote: Right now, the largest opportunity is in logistics

insights.claim: The world's entire supply chain is suboptimal because there is not enough computing to run large-scale efficient optimization calculations.
insights.speaker: John Roese
insights.so_what: Frames a massive latent efficiency gain that quantum could unlock across global supply chains.
insights.quote: The whole supply chain of the world is basically suboptimal because we don't have the computing to run large-scale, efficient optimization calculations

insights.claim: Modeling every road in the United States would not fit in a 1,000-qubit system and might require a million or many millions of qubits.
insights.speaker: John Roese
insights.so_what: Shows the scale gap between today's machines and economically transformative optimization.
insights.quote: You might need a million qubits or many millions to do a big optimization problem.

insights.claim: D-Wave's annealing systems already target optimization and Dell has used annealers in its own supply chain, but annealers are specific to optimization problems.
insights.speaker: John Roese
insights.so_what: Annealing is a present-day niche, while gate-based fault tolerance is needed for broader workloads.

insights.claim: The airline gate problem, with 30 gates, 300 flights and 100,000 passengers on differently configured planes, cascades into so many permutations that supercomputers would need a very long time to solve it.
insights.speaker: John Roese
insights.so_what: A concrete example of combinatorial problems where quantum could deliver operational savings.
insights.quote: I have 30 gates, I have 300 flights, I have 100,000 passengers

insights.claim: FedEx, UPS and DHL rely on rudimentary route heuristics like minimizing left turns because full permutation optimization is infeasible, leaving substantial logistics gains on the table.
insights.speaker: John Roese
insights.so_what: Parcel carriers stand to gain materially from better optimization compute.
insights.quote: That is a very rudimentary optimization, but that's the best they could come up with

insights.claim: By 2030 there may be on the order of a trillion autonomous AI agents, physical and logical, creating environments too complex to model or simulate classically.
insights.speaker: John Roese
insights.so_what: Ties quantum demand to the scaling of agentic AI and autonomous vehicles.
insights.quote: By 2030, how many autonomous agents do you think are going to be in the world?

insights.claim: Autonomous AI agents are predictable individually but become very hard to understand and control when working as systems, and a quantum system could sit in the middle directing a large agent ecosystem.
insights.speaker: John Roese
insights.so_what: Suggests a speculative future role for quantum as a coordination layer for AI systems.
